title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout cote 137, a '½ simplicial' k-module means what is now simply called a simplicial k-module; this follows the old Eilenberg–Zilber usage of 'semi-simplicial'. The next page shows that degeneracies are present, since it uses the Dold–Puppe normalized complex L^! and the Dold–Kan correspondence.

The previous result (Prop., p.7). Suppose the L_n and π_n(L) are projective. Then L is isomorphic to a product
  ∏_{i≥1} Λ^i𝔏⊗M_i × ∏_{j≥0} Λ^j T⊗N_j.
Correspondingly, the normalized complex L^! is a product of elementary complexes:
- (M_i → M_i, identity) sitting in degrees i and i−1;
- N_j placed in degree j.
The pieces are recovered as N_j ≅ H_j and M_i ≅ B_{i−1}.

The building blocks. Reading 𝔏 = Φ_*k and T = Ψ_*k, they are best identified as follows.
- 𝔏 is the reduced free simplicial k-module on Δ^1, i.e. the cone. It is contractible, with 𝔏_n = k^{n+1}.
- T is the reduced free module on S^1 = Δ^1/∂Δ^1, so T = K(k,1) with T_n = k^n.
By Dold–Puppe/Quillen décalage, LΛ^j(M[1]) ≃ LΓ^j(M)[j]. Hence Λ^j T ≃ K(k,j), whose normalized complex is k in degree j. Likewise Λ^i𝔏 has normalized complex (k → k) in degrees i, i−1. Their ranks in degree n are C(n,j) and C(n+1,i) = C(n,i) + C(n,i−1), consistent with the Dold–Kan formula rank L_n = Σ_m C(n,m)·rank N_m.

This page: the Lemma. Assume the L_n and π_n are projective of finite type, and k is commutative with connected spectrum, so ranks are integers. Write μ_i = rank M_i and ν_j = rank N_j. Then
  rank L_n = Σ_i μ_i C(n+1,i) + Σ_j ν_j C(n,j).
The following are equivalent:
- (a) L^! has bounded degrees.
- (b) Only finitely many M_i, N_j are nonzero, so L is a finite direct sum of the Λ^i𝔏⊗M_i and Λ^j T⊗N_j.
- (b') The variant when all f.g. projectives are free (e.g. k a PID or local): L is a finite sum of copies of Λ^i𝔏 and Λ^j T.
- (c) rank L_n is a polynomial in n for n large.
- (d) rank L_n ≤ c·n^N for some N, c and all large n.

Refinement. For fixed N, rank L_n = O(n^N) iff M_i = N_j = 0 for i, j > N. The leading coefficient is then (μ_N + ν_N)/N!.

Proof sketch given. b ⇔ b' and c ⇒ d are trivial; a ⇒ c and d ⇒ a follow from the explicit binomial formula. Each nonzero piece of degree i contributes a polynomial of degree exactly i with positive leading coefficient, so polynomial growth forces boundedness.

Purpose. This classifies 'finite' ∂-perfect simplicial modules by the growth of their ranks. It is a preliminary step towards the dévissage of ∂-perfect complexes and the multiplicative structures (exterior powers Λ^i applied to simplicial modules) named in the cote title.
errors: The margin formula 'lim … / n^N = μ_N + ν_N' needs a factor N! (lim N!·rank L_n/n^N = μ_N + ν_N), since C(n,N) ~ n^N/N!. The page is too faint to tell whether N! is written.

The hypothesis that the π_n are projective is unnecessary for a ⇔ c ⇔ d. By Dold–Kan, L_n = ⊕_{[n]↠[m]} N_m, so projectivity of the L_n alone gives rank L_n = Σ C(n,m) rank N_m. Projectivity of π_n is only needed for the decomposition in (b).
Condition (b') requires that f.g. projectives over k be free ('k principal, plus généralement…'). The text breaks off at exactly this point, so the precise hypothesis is not recorded.

ideas.what: Elementary decomposition of a simplicial module with projective terms and homotopy into Λ^i(cone)⊗M_i and Λ^j K(k,1)⊗N_j
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence plus décalage Λ^j(K(k,1)) ≃ K(k,j); splitting of complexes with projective boundaries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold, Kan, Puppe (1958–61); décalage: Quillen, Illusie (1971)

ideas.what: Bounded normalized complex ⇔ polynomial growth of ranks L_n ⇔ O(n^N) growth, with the degree read off from the growth exponent and the leading coefficient
ideas.modern_name: Rank growth / Hilbert-type function of a simplicial module via the Dold–Kan binomial formula

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine lemma that follows directly from the Dold–Kan rank formula. It is of interest only as a step in Grothendieck's unpublished 1975–76 programme on ∂-perfect simplicial complexes and their multiplicative structures; the page itself contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: '½ simplicial' should be read in the old sense, i.e. simplicial (with degeneracies), not modern semi-simplicial.
'L_n et T_n' in the first line: the hypothesis is on L_n and π_n(L), as in the next page's Prop. ('Supposons les L_n et π_n(L) projectifs de t.f.').
In a), 'L.' probably denotes L^! (the normalized complex), since boundedness refers to the Dold–Puppe complex.
Margin note likely reads 'et on a lim rg_k L_n / n^N = μ_N + ν_N' (possibly with an N! factor), where μ_N = rg M_N and ν_N = rg N_N.
'(M_N + N_N ≠ 0)' in the crossed-out passage refers to N being chosen minimal.
